{{Navbar-GOGPT-tracker}}
'''Manage Seneffe power station''' is a cancelled power station in Manage, Wallonne, Belgium.
It is also known as Manage gas power plant.

==Background==

In February 2021, this project was licensed by the Flemish environmental ministry, and is scheduled to begin construction in 2023.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.brusselstimes.com/208685/permits-granted-for-gas-power-plant-in-manage-wallonia|title=The Brussels Times|website=www.brusselstimes.com|access-date=2022-05-24}}</ref> Eneco highlights that this plant will be able to "switch to green hydrogen in the medium term, as soon as the sustainable production of this fuel and possibilities for the storage and transport are sufficient.<ref name='ref_A'>{{cite web |url=https://www.archyde.com/exit-from-nuclear-power-the-first-license-issued-for-the-manage-gas-power-plant/ |title=Exit from nuclear power: the first license issued for the Manage gas power plant |date=March 24, 2021 |access-date=January 20, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220118082313/https://www.archyde.com/exit-from-nuclear-power-the-first-license-issued-for-the-manage-gas-power-plant/ |archive-date=January 18, 2022 |url-status=live}}</ref>

In September 2023, it was reported that Eneco had abandoned this project stating that "The plant is no longer part of our strategy to be CO2 neutral by 2035 and we are looking for other forms of sustainable flexibility."<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.argusmedia.com/en//news/2492637-eneco-halts-belgian-gas-project|title=Eneco halts Belgian gas project {{!}} Argus Media|date=2023-09-25|website=www.argusmedia.com|language=en|access-date=2024-01-09}}</ref>
